rules.name: Evidence over claims
rules.description: Every fix in this repository must ship with the exact command that proves it, and the report must name what was NOT executed. A run that only shows a green job without loading the artifact proves nothing.

rules.name: No environment variable as transport
rules.description: Do not pass build inputs between layers (host step, container, job level) through environment variables. Set them in the layer where the failing step can already read them; a variable set in the wrong layer is the single most common failure here.

rules.name: A gate must survive its own success
rules.description: A check whose success condition is 'nothing found' must not fail under set -e once it works, and a check must write its verdict where the next layer reads it.

rules.name: No prefix already inside the variable
rules.description: A tag or identifier stored with its own prefix must never be given a second prefix. `cp` + a variable already holding `cp315` builds `cpcp315`, and cibuildwheel silently finds no matching build identifiers.

rules.name: Compute tags in code, not in YAML
rules.description: GitHub expressions have no replace(). Never derive a version or tag inside a workflow expression; compute it in the script that dispatches the build.

rules.name: Build after your feature landed
rules.description: A package can only ship a cp tag for a CPython minor that exists in the interpreter matrix. Never add a wheel target ahead of the interpreter release.

rules.name: Only stdlib in the watcher
rules.description: The CPython watcher must run on the GitHub runner's bare interpreter with no extra installation, so it stays stdlib-only and must keep working with --dry-run.
